statement: Define named rules by criteria (element type, layer, property, classification) that override pen, line type, fill, surface and cut-fill for matching elements in a view.
superiority: Rules apply identically in 2D, 3D and exports and are portable between projects.
notes: VERIFIED — read Graphic Override Rules; named rules with element type plus parameter criteria and an override style (line type, fill type, pens, surface) Acceptance sketch: Rule: walls with FireRating > 60 red; exactly those elements are red in plan and section.

statement: A named combination holds an ordered list of rules saved with a view, and when two rules conflict the one higher in the list wins.
superiority: Conflicts are shown with winning rule.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Graphic Override Combinations; rules apply in list order, a higher rule wins when two cannot both apply; renovation rules sit at the bottom Acceptance sketch: Reordering two overlapping rules changes the result per the order.

statement: Use the same criteria as Find and Select to define overrides.
superiority: One query language across the app.
notes: VERIFIED — read Graphic Override Rules; criteria interface resembles Find and Select but IFC properties are not available Acceptance sketch: Imported criteria produce the same set.

statement: Each override attribute is enabled separately, fill overrides can target drafting, cover or cut fills, and surface overrides can target cut and uncut surfaces.
superiority: Per-channel override with preview.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Graphic Override Rules; fill overrides target drafting, cover or cut fills individually and surface overrides target cut and/or uncut surfaces, each attribute enabled by checkbox Acceptance sketch: Surface override colours 3D only.

statement: A rule can override the line pen, the fill foreground pen and the fill background pen by pen number or colour.
superiority: Pen overrides are resolved at output for exact print match.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Graphic Override Rules; override style has pens (via pen number or colour picker) for fill foreground and background; weight override not documented Acceptance sketch: Override pen = 12 changes cut line colour.

statement: Change line type for outlines of matched elements.

source.ref: Graphic Override Rules; Exceptions: When Overrides Don't Apply

superiority: The same override applies to all views, including section and elevation.
notes: VERIFIED — read Exceptions: When Overrides Don't Apply; line type override works on outlines but skips dimension lines, column symbols, X symbols, frames and handles Acceptance sketch: Override to dashed changes the outline line type of matched walls to the dashed definition in plan and PDF output.

statement: Surface overrides recolour cut and uncut surfaces of matched elements in model views so elements can be colour-coded by any property.
superiority: Colour-blind safe palettes available for colour-coding.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Graphic Override Rules and Graphic Overrides; surface override applies to cut and/or uncut surfaces; used for colour-coding by property Acceptance sketch: Colouring by building material colours 3D and section cut faces identically for the same elements.

statement: The active graphic override combination is stored in each view's settings and can be switched from the quick options bar, except for sections set to manual rebuild or drawing type.
superiority: View inherit chains reduce duplicate settings.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Graphic Overrides; the combination and renovation filter are saved with each view's settings; Quick Options, dialog or Document menu applies it; not available for drawing-type or manual-rebuild section views Acceptance sketch: View A and view B with different combinations display different colours for the same element.

statement: Generate a legend from rules.
superiority: Legend updates live with rules and is placeable on layouts.
notes: REJECTED: no AC30 help page describes a legend generated from graphic override rules (searched Graphic Overrides pages and 'legend' across help; only the Keynote Legend exists) Acceptance sketch: A generated legend lists each rule with its colour and element counts matching the model.

statement: Move rules between projects with conflict handling.
superiority: Rules are stored as versioned JSON for review.
notes: VERIFIED — read Graphic Override Combinations; export/import selected combinations as XML; imported rules merge, same-name different rules get a new suffix Acceptance sketch: Exporting rules and importing into a clean project reproduces ordering and criteria.

statement: Rule with value ranges (e.g. area > 20) colouring heatmap.
superiority: Continuous gradients as well as steps.
notes: UNVERIFIED — help describes rule criteria as like Find & Select (050-120) but cached pages show no numeric range/comparison operators or gradient colouring; Find & Select criteria detail page not in cache Acceptance sketch: Area ranges 0-10, 10-20 map to the configured colours and boundaries colour correctly.

statement: Overrides apply with renovation status.
superiority: Evaluation order is declared and visible.
notes: VERIFIED — read Graphic Overrides By Renovation Status; the three renovation statuses map to predefined override rules editable in the same rules dialog Acceptance sketch: With both active, renovation filter display is applied first then override rules, and the result is reproducible.

statement: Named model view option combinations bundle display options for construction elements, curtain walls, stairs, railings, door and window detail, and other object categories, and are stored with each view.
superiority: Combinations are part of view definition and linked.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Model View Options; combinations cover construction element, curtain wall, stair, railing, door/window detail, elevator, library part and MEP options; saved with views; export/import as XML Acceptance sketch: Switch combination changes display consistently across views.

statement: Display structure as the entire model, without finishes, core only, or with load-bearing elements reduced to their cores, driven by core/finish flags on composite skins and veneers.
superiority: Defined by material classes not just flags.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Partial Structure Display; modes Entire Model, Without Finishes, Core Only, Core of Load-Bearing Elements Only driven by Core/Finish flags on skins and veneers Acceptance sketch: Core only hides finish skins; counts consistent.

statement: Partial structure display acts on composite and profile elements and column veneers, while zones and cover fills ignore it and each mode keeps its own dimensions.

source.ref: Partial Structure Display Settings: Effect on Elements

superiority: Display rules apply per element class.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Partial Structure Display Settings: Effect on Elements; applies to composite/complex elements and column veneers; zones and cover fills unaffected; dimensions are kept per mode Acceptance sketch: Beam core-only display shows only the core skin outline in section.

statement: Show or hide openings, dimension of door/window in plan and opening symbols.

source.ref: Model View Options for Construction Elements

superiority: Per-view setting with preview.
notes: VERIFIED — read Model View Options for Construction Elements; doors/windows shown entire, opening only, with contours or hidden; skylights and openings likewise Acceptance sketch: Hiding openings shows the wall unbroken in plan without altering the model.

statement: Display cut fills as per building material, drawn with fill or with uniform pen.
superiority: Hatch scale is fixed on paper.
notes: VERIFIED — read Model Appearance (Section-Type Views); cut fill of building material, uniform surface colour, or uniform cut pens for cut elements Acceptance sketch: Cut surfaces render with the building material cut fill and pen and not the surface hatch.

statement: A model view option turns the display of zone stamps on or off for a view.

source.ref: Model View Options for Construction Elements

superiority: Zone display options are saved in the view.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Model View Options for Construction Elements; zone panel offers a single Show Zone Stamp switch (off by default); per-category zone display not described Acceptance sketch: Turning zone stamps off in the option combination removes stamps from the view while the zones stay in schedules.

statement: On-screen view options show or hide editing aids such as reference lines, pivot lines, baselines and handles on screen only, without affecting output.
superiority: Construction aids appear only on screen, never in output.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read On-Screen View Options; screen-only toggles for wall/beam reference lines, roof pivot lines, stair baselines, railing reference lines, drafting aids; no effect on output Acceptance sketch: Enabling reference lines draws one line per element in the configured pen.

statement: Up to nine cutting planes, orthogonal, custom or taken from a section line, can cut away the 3D model and are saved with views.
superiority: Interactive gizmo to move and rotate the cut plane.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Create a 3D Cutaway on the Floor Plan or Section; up to 9 cutting planes, orthogonal, custom or from a section line, saved with views; height-based plan cut plane is a separate setting Acceptance sketch: A cutting plane at x = 5 m removes geometry beyond it and leaves a cut face exactly at that plane.

statement: Display options for floor plan cut.
superiority: Cut plane defined per view and per element class.
notes: VERIFIED — read Floor Plan Display (Element Settings); projected with overhead, projected, cut only, symbolic cut, outlines only, overhead all Acceptance sketch: Cut plane at 1.0 m displays the sill-height-dependent window symbol correctly.

statement: Model view options set how much detail doors and windows show in symbols, including minimal-space zones, opening lines and accessories.

source.ref: Detail Level of Door and Window Symbols

superiority: Representation choice is a stored view option.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Detail Level of Door and Window Symbols; detail level, minimal space, opening lines and accessories set in model view options Acceptance sketch: Switching between symbolic and detailed 2D representation changes the object drawing without moving it.

statement: Model view options show or hide curtain wall frames, panels, junctions and accessories and set each to detailed, simplified or schematic display.

source.ref: Model View Options for Curtain Walls

superiority: Display granularity down to individual panel types.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Model View Options for Curtain Walls; frames, panels, junctions, accessories toggled and shown Detailed, Simplified or Schematic (grid lines and boundary); grid lines of other elements not covered Acceptance sketch: Setting panels to hidden and frames to schematic changes plan and 3D output of one curtain wall without altering the element.

statement: Overlapping elements draw by element class and stack level, with commands to bring forward, bring to front, send backward, send to back or reset to the default order.
superiority: A full z-order model with named display layers.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Display Order; default stacking by six element classes plus commands Bring Forward/Front, Send Backward/Back, Reset and 14 stack levels; per-element-type 'sets' not described Acceptance sketch: Moving fill A in front of fill B swaps overdraw so B is hidden where overlapped.

statement: Draw elements in a defined pen priority.

source.ref: Display Order: By Pen Number (Use Color Priority)

superiority: The ordering rule is documented and testable.
notes: REJECTED: no AC30 help page describes drawing priority by pen number; stacking is by element class/stack level (Display Order) and wall/material intersection priority Acceptance sketch: With pen priority enabled the higher pen number draws on top at overlap.

statement: A 3D style chooses the 3D engine and view mode (wireframe, hidden line or shading), with textures available only on the hardware-accelerated engine.
superiority: Real-time physically based shading without engine switching.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read 3D Styles; 3D view mode wireframe, hidden line or shading, texture display depends on engine (hardware acceleration vs vectorial); no sketch mode in 3D styles Acceptance sketch: Switching style changes shading mode and silhouettes with no change to model data.

statement: A 3D style can turn on sun shadow casting, with the sun position derived from the projection's sun settings and the project's geographic location.
superiority: Sun position verified against a published ephemeris.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read 3D Styles and Sun Study; 3D style enables sun shadows (intensity, contours); sun position comes from 3D projection settings and project location settings Acceptance sketch: Shadow length of a 10 m pole at 45 degree sun elevation equals 10 m within 1 percent.

statement: A sketch rendering engine turns the model into a non-photorealistic image with felt-tip, pencil, graphite or marker line styles.
superiority: Stylised sketch as a post-process on exact edges.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Sketch Rendering Engine; a PhotoRendering engine making non-photorealistic felt-tip, pencil, graphite and marker line renderings; not a 3D window style Acceptance sketch: Rendering one model with the sketch engine and the photorealistic engine yields two images from the same geometry.

statement: Select engine used in 3D.
superiority: GPU renderer with deterministic output across hardware.
notes: VERIFIED — read 3D Engines; vectorial engine and hardware acceleration engine chosen via 3D Styles (plus experimental physically based option) Acceptance sketch: The chosen engine persists in the view and the same model renders in each engine.

statement: A 3D style can draw model contours with a quality setting and adjustable line weights, plus silhouette edges on the vectorial engine.
superiority: Analytic curves give crisp silhouettes at any zoom.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read 3D Styles; contours with quality and line-weight sliders (all attached polygons visible) and vectorial-engine silhouettes (single visible polygon) Acceptance sketch: Silhouette edges draw at the configured pen and weight and hidden edges stay hidden.

statement: Use transparency for selected or all elements.
superiority: Order-independent transparency.
notes: VERIFIED — read 3D Styles; Transparency option shows see-through surfaces as transparent in shaded views and is saved with the view Acceptance sketch: Transparency set on a surface blends correctly through two overlapping elements regardless of draw order.

statement: Any viewpoint, view or layout can be shown as a trace reference beneath or alongside the active window, for example the story below, without changing the model.

source.ref: Virtual Trace: Using References to Edit and Compare Model Views and Drawings

superiority: Ghost for any set of stories, filterable by type.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Virtual Trace; any viewpoint, view or layout can be shown as underlay/overlay reference beside or beneath the active window (replaces ghost-story display) Acceptance sketch: Setting the story below as trace reference shows its elements under the active story content and leaves the model unchanged.

statement: Orbit, pan, fly-through, walk-through.
superiority: Consistent navigation scheme across 2D, 3D and layouts, with customizable bindings.
notes: VERIFIED — read Navigation in the 3D Window, Explore Model and Orbit; pan, zoom, orbit and keyboard/mouse explore mode in perspective views Acceptance sketch: Orbit about a picked pivot keeps the pivot fixed in screen space.

statement: The 3D window can show only the selected or marqueed elements, or a limited story range, as a display filter stored with the view.
superiority: Hide state is a view property, saved with it.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Show Selection/Marquee in 3D and Filter and Cut Elements in 3D; show only selected or marqueed elements and a story range in 3D, stored with the view Acceptance sketch: Selecting two walls and using show selection in 3D displays only those two walls in the 3D window.

statement: Named layer combinations store each layer's visibility, lock state and 3D view mode and are saved with each view.
superiority: Per-layer opacity stored in layer combinations.
notes: CORRECTED — statement rewritten to match the page; read Layer Combinations and Layers dialog; combinations store show/hide, lock and 3D view mode (wireframe) per layer and are saved with each view; no per-layer opacity Acceptance sketch: Applying a combination that hides layer A removes its elements from the view while other views keep them.

statement: Graphic override rules can be sorted into rule groups by drag and drop, with search by rule or group name.
superiority: Rule libraries are shareable with tags and versioning.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Graphic Override Rules; Organize Rules in groups, drag and drop, search by name Acceptance sketch: Moving a rule into a group keeps its criteria and style and the group lists it.

statement: Rules in a combination apply in listed order and a higher rule wins when two cannot apply together, while the renovation-based rules always sit at the bottom with the lowest priority.
superiority: The winning rule is shown per element in an inspector.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Graphic Override Combinations; renovation rules fixed at the bottom; order changed by dragging Acceptance sketch: A wall matching a plaster rule and a fire-rating rule takes the colour of whichever rule is higher in the list.

statement: Overrides deliberately skip certain items such as dimension lines, column symbol lines, opening X symbols, drawing frames, text opaque fills and transparent background pens.
superiority: Exceptions are listed in the rule editor so users see them before applying.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Exceptions: When Overrides Don't Apply Acceptance sketch: A line type override applied to walls leaves a dimension line in a plan view unchanged.

statement: Surface-based override criteria match an element only when the surface was assigned through element settings or an object's model panel, not when inherited through connections, solid operations or openings.

source.ref: Surface Criteria in Graphic Override Rules and Collision Detection

superiority: Surface provenance is exposed so criteria always match what users see.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Surface Criteria in Graphic Override Rules and Collision Detection; limited surface recognition for library parts and inherited surfaces Acceptance sketch: A wall whose surface is assigned in its settings matches a surface criterion while one only inheriting a surface from a solid operation does not.

statement: A model view option set can be exported to XML and imported into another project, and the active set shows in the quick options bar.
superiority: Combinations are shareable libraries with a diff on import.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Model View Options Combinations; XML export/import, new duplicates the selected combination, deletion is not undoable Acceptance sketch: Exporting a combination and importing it in a fresh project restores the same options.

statement: Construction element display options set per view whether columns and beams are drawn under slabs with hidden lines, whether beams show contour or axis, and how dividing lines of adjoining slabs appear.

source.ref: Model View Options for Construction Elements

superiority: Each option shows a live preview of the effect.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Model View Options for Construction Elements; column symbol, hidden line under slab, beam contour/axis, slab dividing lines Acceptance sketch: Selecting eliminate lines for two coplanar adjoining slabs removes their dividing line in plan.

statement: A partial structure mode can reduce load-bearing composites to cores while hiding elements classified non-load-bearing or undefined.
superiority: Structural role is a typed element property used by many features.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Partial Structure Display; fourth option core of load-bearing elements only, three stated effects including veneers Acceptance sketch: In load-bearing core mode a non-load-bearing wall disappears and a load-bearing composite shows only its core.

statement: A 3D style bundles engine, view mode, transparency, background, contours and shadows, is saved with a view, updates every view using it when edited, and can be exported and imported as XML.
superiority: Style changes preview across all dependent views before commit.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read 3D Styles; engine, mode, background, contours, shadows; import/export XML Acceptance sketch: Editing a style used by two views changes both views; deleting nothing else changes.

statement: Section-type views can fade distant elements by splitting the view into close and distant zones at a draggable marker line and applying a separate fill to the distant zone.
superiority: Distance bands can be defined numerically and previewed.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Model Appearance (Section-Type Views); fade distant elements with on-screen distant marker line Acceptance sketch: Moving the distant marker past an element changes that element from close to distant fill.

statement: An element's info tag shows which graphic override rules currently affect it, so users can see why it is drawn the way it is.
superiority: The inspector also explains which rules lost and why.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Graphic Overrides; info tag lists rules in effect for the element Acceptance sketch: Hovering the info tag of a wall matched by two rules lists both rules.
